# pickled · llms.txt

Test what agents actually understand about your product.

Pickled is an open-source CLI that tests whether real agents can answer and build with your product (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Anthropic API, OpenAI API), across declared context paths (a source injected, or reached through `web` / `mcp` tools), using deterministic evidence: fact coverage, misstatement rejection, tool-use provenance, and build verification. No LLM grades another LLM.

Install: `bun add -g @pickled-dev/cli`

## Commands

- `pickled init [path]` - scaffold a pickled.yml config in your repo.
- `pickled audit [path]` - static scan of agent-context files (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, llms.txt). No LLM calls.
- `pickled check [path]` - run the questions against the configured agents. `--plan` previews the cells without calling any model.
- `pickled build [path]` - run the builds: the agent edits a workspace and your `verifier` must pass. `--plan` previews cells and executions; `--verify-only` proves each build's harness (preflight + reference control) with no agent runs, reporting `proven` / `unproven` / `broken` per build.
- `pickled test [path]` - score a question's declared example answers against its fact contract, offline. No model calls.
- `pickled report <file>` - re-render a saved receipt from `check --output` or `build --output` as terminal, markdown, or JSON. No model calls.

## Minimum config

```yaml
schemaVersion: 2

product:
  name: your-product
  description: One line about your product.

sources:
  readme: { path: ./README.md }

agents:
  quick:
    provider: claude-code
    model: claude-haiku-4-5

contexts:
  from_readme: { mode: inject, source: readme }

facts:
  install_command:
    statement: your-product installs with bunx your-product.
    match:
      allOf: ["bunx your-product"]

questions:
  - id: install
    question: How do I install your product?
    agents: [quick]
    contexts: [from_readme]
    expects: [install_command]

thresholds:
  questions: 80
```

## Verdict contract

Pickled has two orthogonal verdicts. Renderers must not conflate them.

- **Cell verdict** answers whether one `(agent × context)` cell satisfied its contract. Values: `YES`, `PARTIAL`, `NO`, `Error`. Question cells render as `Well grounded`, `Partially grounded`, `Ungrounded`, or `Error`; builds as `Built`, `Partially built`, `Did not build`, or `Error`.
- **Run verdict** answers whether the run met the configured threshold. Values: `run passes`, `run fails`. Renders only when a threshold is configured. Without a threshold, show `Overall: X / 100` and stop. A thresholded run with any errored cell fails.

The cell verdict determines the label family. A question cell is `YES` only when the scored response fully satisfied the contract; the single-response result and fact coverage are detail, never an upgrade of `PARTIAL`, `NO`, or `Error`. The categorical signal wins.

## Source contract

A registered source is the public context Pickled is allowed to score against: a local file, a URL, or a codebase glob. Anything not registered does not count for scoring. Anything an agent could read can be registered: README, llms.txt, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, hosted docs bundles. Public or private. The id keys the source; declare exactly one of `url` / `path` / `codebase`.

## Contexts: how a source reaches the agent

A task runs as one cell per `(agent × context)` pair. A context is a `mode` plus an optional source:

- `mode: memory` - no source, no tools; measures the model's prior knowledge.
- `mode: inject` - the source content is placed in the prompt; the agent answers from it.
- `mode: web` - web research. On Claude Code the cell scopes built-ins to `[WebSearch, WebFetch]`; on the Anthropic and OpenAI API targets it passes the server-side `web_search` tool. The source is optional (omit for open discovery); nothing is injected.
- `mode: mcp` - declared MCP servers (HTTP). On Claude Code the servers pass to the Agent SDK natively; on the OpenAI API target each becomes a hosted-MCP tool entry. The agent invokes `mcp__<server>__*` tools.

For `web` and `mcp`, a cell that answers without invoking any of its tools is hard-vetoed to `NO`, because an answer from model memory cannot testify to the tool path the cell is meant to test.

To test public docs or llms.txt, compare `memory` against `inject`; add `web` or `mcp` when discovery or tool provenance matters.
## Facts and misstatements

A question scores on two reusable, deterministic registries:

- `facts` - product truths the answer must cover (the coverage axis). Each fact has a `statement` and a `match` (`allOf` substrings must all appear; `anyOf` substrings need one). A question's `expects` lists fact ids.
- `misstatements` - wrong claims the answer must not make (the precision axis). Same `match` shape. A question's `rejects` lists misstatement ids; a matched misstatement is a hard veto. A question with `rejects` requires `examples.pass` and `examples.fail` so the veto is calibrated offline.

The cell verdict is `YES` (all expected facts covered, no misstatement, tool path used), `PARTIAL` (some facts), or `NO`.

## Builds

A build measures whether an agent can BUILD with your context, not just answer. The agent edits a throwaway `workspace` and the cell passes when the `verifier` does. The verifier is SWE-bench-style: `failToPass` commands must fail on the untouched fixture and pass after the agent; optional `passToPass` commands must pass before and after (the regression guard). Each `(agent × context)` cell runs `trials` times in a fresh workspace and reports the pass rate (k of n) as `Built`, `Partially built`, or `Did not build`. An optional `referenceSolution` patch is a positive control: if it is absent, the verifier is marked unproven; if it does not pass on the baseline, the cell errors as broken rather than scoring the agent. Builds run on edit-capable CLI agents (`claude-code`, `codex-cli`) only.

## Agents today

- `claude-code` - Claude Agent SDK. Supports `memory`, `inject`, `web`, and `mcp` contexts.
- `codex-cli` - Codex CLI binary. Supports `memory` and `inject` only.
- `anthropic` - Anthropic API, direct SDK. Requires `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. Supports `memory`, `inject`, and `web` (server-side `web_search`); MCP lands per release.
- `openai` - OpenAI Responses API, direct SDK. Requires `OPENAI_API_KEY`. Supports `memory`, `inject`, `web` (server-side `web_search`), and `mcp` (hosted-MCP, HTTP servers only).

Stubbed and not yet implemented: `amazon-q`, Google API target. Do not list these as supported in present tense.

## JSON contract
JSON output stays raw. It carries machine fields (`verdict`, `passRate`, `meanCoverage`, `verifierProof`). Human labels are derived by the shared report-status helpers, not present in JSON. Default JSON is CI-safe: verdicts, evidence ids, provenance, and build attempts, without full answers, source content, transcripts, diffs, or command output. Use `--verbose` for a forensic receipt. `pickled report file.json --format markdown` is meant for CI job summaries.

## Cost and dry-run controls

For paid agents, a run grows expensive as you add agents and contexts. These flags keep it in check:

- `--plan` (dry run): expand the run, apply filters and sampling, print the cell list, exit. Zero model calls.
- `--max-cells N`: hard fail before any model call if the selected execution count exceeds N. Builds expand by `trials`, so this gates `cells × trials`.
- `--sample N`: deterministic per-task sample.
- `--seed VALUE`: seed for `--sample`. Defaults to the literal string `default` so reruns without `--seed` are reproducible.
- `--task ID`, `--agent NAME`, `--context NAME`: narrow a run by names from `pickled.yml`.

## GitHub Actions

- PRs: run `bunx @pickled-dev/cli test .`, `bunx @pickled-dev/cli check . --plan`, and `bunx @pickled-dev/cli build . --plan`.
- Real agent runs: use `workflow_dispatch`, `schedule`, or trusted branches; pass API keys through secrets; cap with `--max-cells`; save `--output pickled-report.json`; render `pickled report pickled-report.json --format markdown >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"`; upload the JSON receipt as an artifact; do not use `pull_request_target` for paid runs on untrusted fork PRs.

Read more: https://github.com/caiopizzol/pickled · https://docs.pickled.dev/pickled-yml
